packet_dag.terminal_condition: One Time Operations shows Classes & Content as the sidebar category, renders a compact One Time section rail, keeps mobile rail scrolling without page overflow, and records verification evidence before deploy closeout.

title: One Time Operations Content IA And Section Rail

reasons: Operator reported the Rabbi / One Time section was missing a clear content area.
Operator called out repetitive top categories, subcategories, and filters.
The correction is presentation and IA scoped to the Operations shell and existing content routes.
The change is app-visible and therefore requires deploy/live-smoke closeout.
affected_product_surfaces: One Time Operations content section rail
likely_external_provider_blockers: Production live smoke requires Operations auth in the target environment.
Railway deployment or GitHub publication can be blocked by branch or auth state.
ramble_router.next_exact_packet: After this scoped fix is deployed, use the Agent Mode audit results to create a separate cross-app toolbar/filter consistency packet if concrete defects remain.

operator_intent_summary: Make the Rabbi / One Time Operations information architecture clearer by exposing Classes & Content as a main category, using compact content subsections at the top, and preserving mobile horizontal section navigation without repetitive tabs.
raw_quotes: the categories and subcategories and filters don't really logically make sense
the filters and the subcategories and top they're very repetitive
on mobile they should like slide
it should be consistent across like our entire app

decisions_captured.decision: Use existing route ids for content sections; label `research` as Source Prep in One Time instead of migrating data or URLs.

out_of_scope: No backend authorization, database schema, route access policy, action registry policy, payment/access, DNS, email, WhatsApp, Telegram, Drive, Vimeo, Zoom, provider-account, or production-data mutation.
No external send, publish, upload, access grant, or payment action.
No GHL runtime, LeadConnector runtime, external CRM write, or external provider setup.
No broad redesign of student, parent, public, provider portal, or non-One-Time content surfaces in this packet.

inspection_targets: public/operations.html CONTENT_SUBTABS, PROVIDER_PROGRAM_SUBTABS, currentSubnavConfig, renderTopFilterRail, workspaceNavItems, normalizeCurrentRouteForWorkspace, setCurrentSection, renderContent, renderProviderProgramWorkspace
tests/one-time-operations-ui-smoke.test.js current One Time nav and mobile checks
known_blockers: Live deploy and authenticated live smoke still need to run after publication.
Full cross-app toolbar consistency remains broader than this scoped One Time fix.
observed_visual_defects: Sidebar label `Classes` did not make the content workspace obvious.
Classes & Content durable IA defaulted to a stale schedule subsection.
One Time content rail included generic production tabs that are not primary Rabbi-facing subsections.
Provider Program rail used long repetitive labels.
Mobile rail had avoidable vertical height from the meta row.

expanded_phrases.consistent: Use the same side-category plus top-section rail pattern already established in Operations: main work areas in the sidebar and compact subsections in the top rail.
expanded_phrases.professional: Use concise section labels, avoid implementation terms in primary navigation, keep readable controls, and prove desktop/mobile no-overflow behavior.
expanded_phrases.logic: Group content work by user task: Library, Meeting Drops, Source Prep, Bundles.
expanded_phrases.repetitive: Do not expose workflow/status/output tabs as top-level One Time sections when they duplicate deeper filters or Studio workflows.
expanded_phrases.mobile: Keep the top rail horizontally scrollable, non-wrapping, and compact enough for a 390px viewport.
expanded_phrases.filters: Treat the global top rail as section navigation; leave detailed filters inside the view's filter panel.

product_quality_expansion.first_party_pattern_interpretation: This packet uses first-party BNA Operations IA only. No external CRM/provider runtime or data mutation is part of the correction.

requirements.statement: Expose Classes & Content as the One Time sidebar category for content work.
requirements.expected_result: The One Time sidebar item opens the existing content view at `one_time_library` and the durable IA default is `library`.
acceptance_criteria: The content route remains scoped to `rabbi_sheller_provider` / `one_time_mishnah_class`.

requirements.statement: Use a compact One Time content section rail.
requirements.expected_result: The One Time content rail shows exactly Library, Meeting Drops, Source Prep, and Bundles.
acceptance_criteria: The rail does not show `selected`, `repurpose`, `newsletter`, or `prompts` in One Time scope.
Generic content tabs remain available outside One Time where applicable.

requirements.statement: Keep the One Time mobile top rail horizontally scrollable without page overflow.
requirements.expected_result: At 390px width, the content rail is `overflow-x:auto`, `flex-wrap:nowrap`, hides the meta row, and does not widen the page.
acceptance_criteria: Focused browser smoke verifies mobile rail ids and computed styles.
Document scroll width stays within viewport width plus one pixel.
No console errors are emitted during the route smoke.

requirements.statement: Shorten provider Program sections and provide a Content bridge.
requirements.expected_result: Provider Program uses compact section labels and a Content panel that links to the real Classes & Content workspace sections.
acceptance_criteria: Program rail includes `Content` as a top section.
Content bridge exposes Library, Meeting Drops, Source Prep, and Bundles.
No backend, auth, data, or external-provider behavior changes.

criteria: Raw operator wording is captured in `RAW-20260706-956`.
Affected workspace/project and exact Operations routes are named.
Current-state code paths for nav items, section rail, content tabs, and provider Program tabs were inspected.
The correction is scoped to presentation/IA and tests.
External writes and backend/data behavior are explicitly out of scope.
